items.title: Every invertible sheaf on the source of a finite morphism that is an isomorphism outside a discrete set is pulled back from the target
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a finite morphism f : X -> Y that is an isomorphism over an open V whose complement is discrete, the pullback map on Picard groups is surjective. The proof identifies Pic with H^1 of the unit sheaf, runs the Leray spectral sequence for O_X^*, observes that the edge map H^1(X, O_X^*) -> H^0(Y, R^1 f_*O_X^*) is zero by the cited divisor-trivialization lemma, so that H^1(X, O_X^*) = H^1(Y, f_*O_X^*), and then breaks O_Y^* -> f_*O_X^* into two short exact sequences whose kernel and cokernel are supported on the discrete complement, where higher cohomology vanishes (proof lines 7953-7986). H2: the two-step surjectivity argument through the Leray edge map and the vanishing on discrete supports is the substance.
